messages.text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?

I need the trailer for my home project within the next few weeks. I don’t have exact dates or a firm duration yet; it’s for this project, not a recurring need. A fair arrangement gives each of us a scheduled turn soon—I’m not willing to wait until A is completely done. Yes, I’ll talk with A about dates. I’m fine with writing down the agreement and sharing it; costs and the pad arrangement still need discussion.

Thanks for asking. The trailer is taking up space, and I’d prefer it not stay on my pad much longer, though I don’t have an exact date in mind and don’t need turns using it. I rent, and my landlord would need to approve a change to what’s kept on the pad; I haven’t asked him yet, so I can’t promise a schedule. I agree the pad shouldn’t become an unpaid burden for me.

I’d prefer it gone from my pad for good, though a short stay might be fine if my landlord approves. I haven’t asked him yet, and I’m not sure how quickly he’d answer. Asking once we have a clearer plan would probably be easier. Sharing any moving cost seems fair to discuss, but we haven’t decided that.

I need it for weekend trips starting in the next few weeks. I don’t have exact dates or trip lengths yet. I expect to use it on more than one weekend, but I haven’t set a repeating schedule. The dates can move somewhat, but I need this settled within a few weeks. Fair means a clear schedule that gives each of us access without having to get permission each time. Writing it down and settling costs beforehand makes sense; I don’t know the price or shares yet.

Yes, I’ll put my dates in writing first once I check my project schedule. I’ll talk with A at work to pin down dates. Let’s set a reasonable deadline within the next few weeks so this doesn’t stall. I don’t agree to an automatic three-way split of all costs; we haven’t decided that.

I need it for weekend trips. I don’t have exact dates or trip lengths yet; I expect to use it on multiple weekends, but don’t have a fixed repeating schedule. I have some flexibility, but need a plan within the next few weeks. I’m open to two shorter turns if we agree on dates that still let me use it soon. Fair means a clear schedule and reliable access without needing permission each time. The list sounds reasonable; costs and shares still need to be worked out.
March 13 works. The list looks right. Add how overlapping date requests will be resolved before anything is booked.

I’m open to C going first if my weekend trips still fit in the same few weeks. Talking with C at work is fine for pinning down dates. A written deadline for naming dates makes sense, but I won’t agree yet to splitting every cost three ways—we need to decide costs and shares together. The calendar should stay tentative until B has the landlord’s answer.
A short note might help, as long as I can review it before it’s sent. The list sounds right to me; I don’t think anything is missing.

I can name my dates by March 13. The overlap rule isn’t fair as written: being first to submit shouldn’t decide who gets the days, especially when C is already going first. If dates conflict, we should talk and choose an arrangement that preserves one turn each before either gets a second.

The order works—I need my turn early, not after A’s weekends. I don’t agree that whoever writes first automatically gets overlapping days; resolve conflicts together, or use a neutral tie-breaker. Nothing should be treated as booked until we agree and B’s landlord answers.
